reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Traffic violation records, dispositions, and retention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 4; Model Traffic Ordinance). Requires the police department or traffic division to keep records of all charged city traffic ordinance and state vehicle law violations and final dispositions, showing violation types and totals, accumulating and maintained complete for at least the most recent five-year period.

headings.title: Serially numbered forms and disposal records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 4). Requires violation record and notice forms to be serially numbered and mandates a monthly and annual public written record showing the disposal of all such forms.

headings.title: Public record status of records and reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 4). Designates all such violation records and reports as public records.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 4) and verified source identity and all fingerprints. Confirmed five-year accumulation/retention scope, serial numbering and monthly/annual disposal logs, and public-record status; retained all three draft titles.

headings.title: Office establishment and designated city official
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 11; Model Traffic Ordinance). Establishes the office of city traffic engineer and designates the city engineer or other designated city official to serve in addition to other functions and exercise traffic powers and duties under the ordinance.

headings.title: City traffic engineer powers and duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 11). Lists duties of the city traffic engineer covering installation, timing, and maintenance of traffic control devices, engineering accident analyses and remedial measures, traffic condition investigations, traffic operations planning, inter-official cooperation, and additional ordinance duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 11) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed distinction between establishing/designating the office and enumerating traffic engineering duties; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Implementing, temporary, and experimental regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 12). Empowers the chief of police, with approval of the city traffic engineer, to make regulations implementing city traffic ordinances and to make and enforce temporary or experimental regulations for emergencies or special conditions, limiting temporary or experimental regulations to ninety days.

headings.title: Testing traffic control devices under actual conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 12). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to test traffic control devices under actual traffic conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 12) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed chief-of-police rulemaking with traffic-engineer approval and 90-day temporary/experimental limit in subsection 1 and device testing in subsection 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Commission establishment, membership, and chairman
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 13). Establishes an uncompensated traffic commission with specified ex officio city officials, city engineer and city attorney office representatives, and additional city officers and unofficial-body representatives appointed by the mayor, who also appoints and may remove the chairman.

headings.title: Commission duties, recommendations, and funding limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 13). Defines the traffic commission's duties and authority, qualified as within the limits of available funds, to coordinate traffic activities, supervise traffic report preparation and publication, receive traffic complaints, and recommend improvements to city legislative and administrative officials.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 13) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed uncompensated membership/mayor chairman appointment in subsection 1 and the available-funds qualification on commission authority in subsection 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Police duty to enforce traffic laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 14, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Assigns police department officers, or officers assigned by the chief of police, the duty to enforce city traffic laws and applicable state vehicle laws within the city.

headings.title: Police authority to direct traffic
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Police traffic direction and emergency authority" so the proviso is not narrowed to emergencies alone. Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 14, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Authorizes police officers to direct traffic by voice, hand, or signal in conformance with traffic laws, with a proviso allowing direction as conditions require notwithstanding traffic laws during fires or other emergencies, to expedite traffic, or to safeguard pedestrians.

headings.title: Fire officer traffic direction at incident scenes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 14, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Authorizes fire department officers at the scene of an incident to direct or assist police in directing traffic at the scene or in the immediate vicinity.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 14, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 2 to "Police authority to direct traffic" so the proviso covering fires, emergencies, expediting traffic, and safeguarding pedestrians is not narrowed to emergencies alone; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Qualifying situations for emergency vehicle privileges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 20, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032, A.L. 2025 H.B. 225). Authorizes drivers of authorized emergency vehicles to exercise section privileges, subject to section conditions, when responding to an emergency call, pursuing an actual or suspected law violator, or responding to—but not returning from—a fire alarm.

headings.title: Permitted privileges and safety conditions
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Permitted driving privileges and safety conditions" to cover subdivision (1) parking or standing alongside driving privileges in (2)–(4). Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)–(4) and history note (A.L. 2025 H.B. 225). Lists conditional privileges for authorized emergency vehicle drivers: parking or standing regardless of ordinance, proceeding past red/stop signals or signs after slowing for safe operation, exceeding speed limits without endangering life or property, and disregarding direction or turning rules.

headings.title: Audible and visual signal requirements and police exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note (A.L. 2025 H.B. 225). Conditions emergency-vehicle exemptions while in motion on sounding a siren or displaying a 500-foot front red light or a flashing blue light authorized under § 307.175, while exempting police vehicles from signals during highway speeding-evidence gathering, suspected crimes in progress where signals risk evidence destruction or escape, or criminal vehicle surveillance.

headings.title: Duty of due regard and reckless disregard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 2025 H.B. 225). States that the section does not relieve an authorized emergency vehicle driver from the duty to drive with due regard for all persons' safety or protect against consequences of reckless disregard for others' safety.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including subdivisions 2(1)–(4) and 3(1)–(3) and history note (through A.L. 2025 H.B. 225), and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed fire-alarm return exclusion in 1, § 307.175 blue-light reference and police signal exceptions in 3, and due-regard/reckless-disregard rule in 4. Revised subsection 2 to "Permitted privileges and safety conditions" to include parking/standing; retained subsections 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Yielding and stopping for approaching emergency vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 21, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Requires other drivers, except when otherwise directed by a police officer, to yield right-of-way, pull parallel and close to the right edge or curb clear of intersections, and stop until an approaching emergency vehicle using lawful audible and visual signals—or a police vehicle lawfully using an audible signal only—has passed.

headings.title: Emergency driver duty of due regard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 21, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Preserves the authorized emergency vehicle driver's duty to drive with due regard for the safety of all highway users.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 21, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed police-direction exception and police audible-only signal rule in subsection 1 and emergency-driver due-regard duty in subsection 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Occupant immediate accident notice under 300.110
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 24). Requires a capable vehicle occupant at the time of an accident to give or cause to be given the immediate accident notice required under § 300.110 whenever the driver is physically incapable of doing so.

headings.title: Owner written accident report under 300.115
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 24). Requires the vehicle owner, if not the driver, to file the written accident report required under § 300.115 within five days after the accident whenever the driver is physically incapable of making it.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 24) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed exact cross-references to § 300.110 (occupant immediate notice) and § 300.115 (non-driver owner five-day written report); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Presumption of lawful placement of devices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 30). Establishes a rebuttable presumption, absent competent contrary evidence, that official traffic control devices placed in approximate conformity with the ordinance were placed by official act or direction of lawful authority.

headings.title: Presumption of ordinance compliance for devices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 30). Establishes a rebuttable presumption, absent competent contrary evidence, that official traffic control devices placed under the ordinance and purporting to conform comply with ordinance requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 30) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed both presumptions are rebuttable by competent contrary evidence and distinguished lawful placement (1) from ordinance compliance (2); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Obedience to flashing red and yellow signals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(2) and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 33). Sets vehicular obedience rules for illuminated flashing red stop signals (stop before crosswalk, limit line, or intersection and follow stop-sign rules) and flashing yellow caution signals (proceed only with caution).

headings.title: Railroad crossing exclusion and 300.295 governance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 33). Excludes railroad grade crossings from this section and cross-references § 300.295 to govern driver conduct approaching railroad grade crossings.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(2) and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 33) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed flashing red/yellow rules in 1 and railroad grade crossing exclusion with § 300.295 cross-reference in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Authority to mark roadway traffic lanes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/footnote notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 40). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to mark traffic lanes on streets or highways where regular alignment of traffic is necessary.

headings.title: Staying within marked lanes and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 40; footnote: '*Word "marking" appears in original rolls.' keyed to 'making*'). Prohibits vehicle operators from failing or refusing to stay within marked lane boundaries except when lawfully passing or preparatory to making a lawful turn; retains the original-rolls textual discrepancy explicitly.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 40 and original-rolls footnote "*Word 'marking' appears in original rolls." keyed to "making*" in subsection 2) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed passing and turning exceptions and preserved the source discrepancy explicitly without inventing corrections; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Authority to place intersection turning markers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 44). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to place markers, buttons, or signs within or adjacent to intersections indicating vehicle turning courses that may conform to or differ from courses otherwise prescribed by law or ordinance.

headings.title: Obedience to intersection turning markers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 44). Prohibits vehicle drivers from disobeying authorized turning markers, buttons, or other indications placed within an intersection.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 44) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed authority to place markers/buttons/signs within or adjacent to intersections in 1 and driver obedience rule in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Designating reversible streets and temporary directional lanes
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Designating reversible and temporary directional lanes" to reflect that reversible period designations apply to streets and parts of streets as well as specific lanes. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 50). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to designate streets, parts of streets, or specific lanes for opposite directional movement during different periods of the day with notice markings, signs, barriers, or devices, and to erect signs temporarily designating directional lanes regardless of the roadway center line.

headings.title: Prohibition on violating directional traffic devices
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Prohibition on violating directional lane devices" so scope matches street, street-part, and lane designations under subsection 1. Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 50). Makes it unlawful to operate any vehicle in violation of markings, signs, barriers, or other devices placed under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 50) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Designating reversible streets and temporary directional lanes" and subsection 2 to "Prohibition on violating directional traffic devices" to reflect applicability to streets and parts of streets as well as lanes.

headings.title: Stopping location when required at yield signs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 54). Specifies where a driver approaching a yield sign must stop if required for safety to stop: before the near crosswalk, at a marked stop line, or at the nearest point with a view of approaching intersecting traffic.

headings.title: Stopping locations at stop signs and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 54). Requires drivers approaching stop-sign intersections, except when directed to proceed by a police officer or traffic control signal, to stop before the near crosswalk, at a marked stop line, or at the nearest point with a view of approaching intersecting traffic.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 54) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed conditional "if required for safety to stop" qualification for yield signs in 1 and police/signal exceptions for stop signs in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Stopping distance and conditions for approaching trains
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 60). Requires drivers approaching railroad grade crossings to stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the nearest rail and wait until safe to proceed when a visible warning signal, lowered gate or flagman, or plainly visible train in hazardous proximity indicates an approaching train.

headings.title: Prohibition on bypassing closed or moving gates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 60). Prohibits driving any vehicle through, around, or under a railroad crossing gate or barrier while it is closed or being opened or closed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(3) and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 60) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed 15-to-50-foot stopping range and three triggering conditions in 1 and closed/moving gate bypass ban in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Motorcycle operator and passenger seating requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 70, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80). Requires motorcycle operators to ride only on the permanent regular seat and restricts carrying passengers to motorcycles designed for more than one person with a two-person regular seat or firmly attached rear or side seat.

headings.title: Motorized bicycle seating, passengers, and footrests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 70, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80). Requires motorized bicycle operators to ride astride the permanent regular seat, bars carrying more than one person unless so designed, and requires a passenger seat and footrests on multi-person motorized bicycles.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 70, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed distinction between motorcycle seating (1) and motorized bicycle seating/footrests (2); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Bicycles prohibited on business-district sidewalks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 109, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80). Prohibits riding a bicycle on a sidewalk within a business district.

headings.title: Yielding and signaling to pedestrians on sidewalks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 109, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80). Requires any person riding a bicycle on a sidewalk to yield right-of-way to pedestrians and give an audible signal before overtaking and passing a pedestrian.

headings.title: Motorized bicycles prohibited on sidewalks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 109, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80). Prohibits riding a motorized bicycle on any sidewalk.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 109, A.L. 1980 H.B. 995 & 1051; Effective 6-20-80) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed business-district bicycle ban (1), pedestrian yielding/signaling (2), and blanket motorized bicycle sidewalk ban (3); retained all three draft titles.

headings.title: All-terrain vehicles on streets and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1279, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Prohibits operating all-terrain vehicles (§ 300.010) on city streets and highways except for government official use, daytime agricultural or industrial on-premises use, or city special permits under § 304.013.

headings.title: Off-road vehicles in waterways, exceptions, and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1279, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Prohibits operating off-road vehicles (§ 304.001—distinct from all-terrain vehicles in subsection 1) in city streams or rivers, with landowner, agricultural-permission, and customary or highway road-crossing fording exceptions, and directs enforcement by state and political-subdivision peace officers within their jurisdictions.

headings.title: Street-exception licensing, speed, and safety flag rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1279, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Requires a valid state motor vehicle license (without motorcycle exam), speeds under thirty miles per hour, and a specified seven-foot rear day-glow triangular bicycle safety flag when operating an all-terrain vehicle on a street or highway under a section exception.

headings.title: Careless operation, impairment, and under-eighteen helmet rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)–(3) and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1279, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Prohibits operating an all-terrain vehicle carelessly so as to endanger persons or property, while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances, or without a securely fastened safety helmet for operators or towed/propelled individuals under age eighteen.

headings.title: Passenger prohibition and agricultural exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1279, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Prohibits an all-terrain vehicle operator from carrying a passenger except for agricultural purposes.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1279, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032). Classifies a violation of this section as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including subdivisions 1(1)–(3) and 4(1)–(3) and history note (L. 1988 H.B. 990 through A.L. 2002 H.B. 1270 and H.B. 2032), and verified source identity and fingerprints. Verified critical distinction between § 300.010 all-terrain vehicles (subsections 1, 3–5) and § 304.001 off-road vehicles in streams/rivers (subsection 2), plus § 304.013 permits, under-18 helmet rule, agricultural passenger exception, and class C misdemeanor penalty; retained all six draft titles.

headings.title: Driver yielding at unsignalized crosswalks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 82). Requires drivers to yield right-of-way, slowing or stopping as needed, to pedestrians in crosswalks when traffic control signals are absent or not operating, if the pedestrian is on the driver's half of the roadway or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger.

headings.title: Pedestrians suddenly entering a vehicle's path
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 82). Prohibits pedestrians from suddenly leaving a curb or place of safety and walking or running into the path of a vehicle too close for the driver to yield.

headings.title: Exception for conditions under 300.390(2)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 82). States that subsection 1 does not apply under the pedestrian-tunnel or overhead-crossing conditions stated in subsection 2 of § 300.390.

headings.title: Prohibition on passing vehicles stopped at crosswalks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 82). Prohibits drivers approaching from the rear from overtaking and passing a vehicle stopped at a marked crosswalk or unmarked intersection crosswalk for a crossing pedestrian.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 82) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed unsignalized crosswalk scope in 1, sudden entry rule in 2, exact § 300.390(2) cross-reference in 3, and rear-passing prohibition in 4; retained all four draft titles.

headings.title: Yielding when crossing outside crosswalks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 85). Requires pedestrians crossing a roadway outside a marked crosswalk or unmarked intersection crosswalk to yield right-of-way to all vehicles on the roadway.

headings.title: Yielding where tunnels or overhead crossings exist
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 85). Requires pedestrians crossing a roadway at a point where a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing is provided to yield right-of-way to all vehicles on the roadway.

headings.title: Inapplicability to crossings prohibited under 300.395
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 85). States that subsections 1 and 2 do not apply under § 300.395 conditions where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at designated places.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 85) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed outside-crosswalk yielding (1), tunnel/overhead crossing yielding (2), and § 300.395 inapplicability cross-reference (3); retained all three draft titles.

headings.title: Crossing between adjacent signalized intersections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 86). Prohibits pedestrians from crossing outside a crosswalk between adjacent intersections with operating traffic control signals.

headings.title: Crossing outside crosswalks in business districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 86). Prohibits pedestrians from crossing a roadway outside a crosswalk in any business district.

headings.title: Crossing outside crosswalks on ordinance-designated streets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 86). Prohibits pedestrians from crossing a roadway outside a crosswalk on any street designated by ordinance.

headings.title: Diagonal intersection crossings and device authorization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 86). Prohibits pedestrians from crossing a roadway intersection diagonally unless authorized by official traffic control devices, and requires compliance with those devices when authorized.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 86) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed distinct crossing restrictions across adjacent signalized intersections, business districts, ordinance-designated streets, and diagonal crossings with device authorization; retained all four draft titles.

headings.title: Pedestrian obedience to bridge operation signals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 87). Prohibits pedestrians from entering or remaining on a bridge or approach beyond a bridge signal, gate, or barrier after a bridge operation signal indication is given.

headings.title: Bypassing railroad or bridge gates prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 87). Prohibits pedestrians from passing through, around, over, or under a crossing gate or barrier at a railroad grade crossing or bridge while closed or being opened or closed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 87) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed bridge-signal obedience in 1 and railroad/bridge closed or moving gate bypass ban in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Roadway walking prohibited where sidewalks exist
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 88). Makes it unlawful for a pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway where sidewalks are provided.

headings.title: Walking facing traffic where no sidewalks exist
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 88). Requires pedestrians walking along a highway without sidewalks, when practicable, to walk only on the left side of the roadway or shoulder facing oncoming traffic.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 88) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed adjacent-roadway ban where sidewalks exist (1) and "when practicable" left-side facing-traffic rule where none exist (2); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Designating angle parking and state commission approval
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Designating angle parking and state highway approval" to reflect commission resolution/order approval required for both federal-aid and state highways. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 113). Directs the city traffic engineer to determine and mark or sign streets for angle parking, prohibiting angle parking on federal-aid or state highways without a state highways and transportation commission resolution or order finding sufficient roadway width without interfering with free traffic movement.

headings.title: Restrictions protecting passing traffic and streetcar tracks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 113). Prohibits indicating or permitting angle parking where passing traffic would be caused or required to drive on the left side of the street or on streetcar tracks.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 113) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Designating angle parking and state commission approval" to cover both federal-aid and state highways requiring commission resolution/order approval; retained subsection 2 covering left-side driving and streetcar tracks.

headings.title: Issuance and eligibility for curb-backing permits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 115). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to issue special permits to real-property owners or lessees or vehicle owners allowing vehicles to back to the curb for loading or unloading merchandise or materials, subject to permit terms and conditions.

headings.title: Violation of special permit terms prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 115). Makes it unlawful for any permittee or other person to violate any special terms or conditions of a curb-backing loading permit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 115) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed permit issuance/eligibility (real-property owner/lessee or vehicle owner) in 1 and prohibition on violating permit terms in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Exemption where sufficient light provides visibility
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Exemption where street lighting provides sufficient visibility" to match statutory "sufficient light" wording without narrowing to street lighting. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 116). Exempts lawfully parked vehicles from displaying nighttime lights (half hour after sunset to half hour before sunrise) when sufficient light reveals persons or objects within five hundred feet.

headings.title: Nighttime lamp requirements and motor-driven cycle exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 116). Requires vehicles parked or stopped at night on poorly lit roadways or shoulders (attended or unattended) to display 500-foot front white/amber and rear red lamps positioned near passing traffic, with an explicit exclusion for motor driven cycles.

headings.title: Dimming lighted headlamps on parked vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 116). Requires any lighted headlamps on a parked vehicle to be depressed or dimmed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 116) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Exemption where sufficient light provides visibility" to match statutory "sufficient light" text without narrowing to street lighting; retained subsections 2 (preserving the motor-driven cycle exclusion) and 3.

headings.title: Prohibited stopping, standing, and parking locations and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Prohibited locations for stopping, standing, and parking" to preserve the opening general exceptions and tier-specific passenger and loading/unloading exceptions. Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)(a)–(i), (2)(a)–(f), and (3)(a)–(b) and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 117). Sets general exceptions (avoiding traffic conflict, law, police officer, or official device) and three location-prohibition tiers: stopping/standing/parking, standing/parking (with momentary passenger pickup/discharge exception), and parking (with temporary loading/unloading exception). Retains literal Model Traffic Ordinance parentheticals "(traffic authority)" in (1)(e) and "(when properly signposted)" in (2)(e).

headings.title: Moving vehicles without lawful control into unlawful positions
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Moving another's vehicle into prohibited areas" to cover both prohibited areas and unlawful curb distances and match "not lawfully under his control". Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 117). Prohibits moving a vehicle not lawfully under one's control into a prohibited area or an unlawful distance away from a curb.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions 1(1)(a)–(i), 1(2)(a)–(f), and 1(3)(a)–(b) and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 117), and verified source identity and fingerprints. Preserved literal Model Traffic Ordinance parentheticals "(traffic authority)" in 1(1)(e) and "(when properly signposted)" in 1(2)(e). Revised subsection 1 to "Prohibited stopping, standing, and parking locations and exceptions" and subsection 2 to "Moving vehicles without lawful control into unlawful positions".

headings.title: Authority to post no-parking signs near schools
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 122). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to erect no-parking signs on either or both sides of streets adjacent to school property when parking would interfere with traffic or create a hazardous situation.

headings.title: Obedience to posted school no-parking signs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 122). Prohibits parking a vehicle in designated places where official school-adjacent no-parking signs have been erected under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 122) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed sign-erection authority adjacent to school property (1) and obedience requirement once official signs are erected (2); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Authority to post narrow-street no-parking signs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 123). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to erect no-parking signs on streets with roadways up to twenty feet wide, or on one side of streets with roadways up to thirty feet wide.

headings.title: Obedience to narrow-street no-parking signs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 123). Prohibits parking a vehicle on a narrow street in violation of official no-parking signs erected under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 123) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed 20-foot and 30-foot roadway-width sign authority (1) and obedience requirement (2); retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Authority to designate hazardous or congested places
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Authority to sign hazardous or congested zones" to avoid the ambiguous verb "sign" and match statutory wording. Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 126). Authorizes the city traffic engineer to determine and designate by proper signs places up to one hundred feet long where stopping, standing, or parking would create an especially hazardous condition or unusual traffic delay.

headings.title: Obedience to signs at hazardous or congested places
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 126). Prohibits stopping, standing, or parking a vehicle in any hazardous or congested place where official signs are erected under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 126) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 1 to "Authority to designate hazardous or congested places" to avoid the ambiguous verb "sign" and match statutory wording; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Bus standing and parking limited to stands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 132). Prohibits bus operators from standing or parking a bus on any street outside a designated bus stand.

headings.title: Bus loading locations and emergency exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 132). Prohibits bus operators from stopping on streets to load or unload passengers or baggage outside designated bus stops, bus stands, or passenger loading zones, except in an emergency.

headings.title: Bus curb positioning when loading or unloading
headings.reviewNote: Revised during review from "Curb positioning for buses loading passengers" to cover loading or unloading both passengers and baggage. Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 132). Requires bus operators entering designated stops, stands, or loading zones to stop with the right front wheel within eighteen inches of the curb and approximately parallel to the curb so as not to unduly impede traffic.

headings.title: Taxicab stands and temporary loading exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 132). Prohibits taxicab operators from standing or parking on streets outside designated taxicab stands, while allowing temporary stops complying with other regulations when actively engaged in expeditious passenger loading or unloading.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 132) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Revised subsection 3 to "Bus curb positioning when loading or unloading" to cover both passengers and baggage; retained subsections 1, 2 (emergency exception), and 4 (taxicab temporary loading exception).

headings.title: Options to pay fine or plead not guilty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 144). Gives persons charged with bureau-payable traffic offenses the option to plead guilty, waive court appearance, and pay the fine at the traffic violations bureau within the specified time, or deposit lawful bail, plead not guilty, and receive a trial.

headings.title: Effect of fine payment and bureau receipt
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 144). Deems payment of a fine to the traffic violations bureau an acknowledgment of conviction and requires the bureau to issue a payment receipt upon accepting the prescribed fine.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1965 p. 445 § 144) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed guilty-plea/fine option vs. bail/not-guilty trial option in 1 and conviction acknowledgment/receipt requirement in 2; retained both draft titles.

headings.title: Municipal uniform traffic ticket books under Rule 37.46
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 150, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634; Effective 1-02-79). Requires the municipality to provide uniform traffic ticket books containing serially numbered quadruplicate citation sets in the form prescribed by archived statutory reference to Supreme Court Rule 37.46.

headings.title: Issuance to police chief, records, and court filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 150, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634; Effective 1-02-79). Requires ticket books to be issued to the chief of police or authorized agent with maintained issuance records and written receipts, and authorizes municipal ordinance violation judges to require filing copies of records and receipts with the court.

headings.title: Police chief issuance to officers and tracking records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 150, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634; Effective 1-02-79). Makes the chief of police responsible for issuing ticket books to individual police department members, requiring written receipts, and maintaining records of every book and each citation set contained therein.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and source notes (L. 1965 p. 445 § 150, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634; Effective 1-02-79) and verified source identity and fingerprints. Confirmed archived statutory reference to Supreme Court Rule 37.46 in subsection 1 is retained neutrally without claiming current rule status, and confirmed issuance/record distinctions between subsections 2 and 3; retained all three draft titles.
